example
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (C : ℝ)
    (hLSI : ∀ (v : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ∞ v → HasCompactSupport v →
      (∫ x, (v x)^2 * Real.log ((v x)^2) ∂μ) -
        (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
      2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient v x‖^2 ∂μ)
    (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hs : HasCompactSupport f) :
    Poincare.Admissible μ f ∧ Poincare.variance μ f ≤ C * Poincare.dirichletEnergy μ f := by
  have hfi : Integrable f μ := hf.continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hs
  let c : ℝ := ∫ x, f x ∂μ
  let g : E → ℝ := fun x => f x - c
  have hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g := hf.sub contDiff_const
  have hgi : Integrable g μ := hfi.sub (integrable_const c)
  have hmean : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) = 0 := by
    rw [integral_sub hfi (integrable_const c), integral_const]
    simp [c]
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := hs.isCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hf.continuous.continuousOn
  have hfb (x : E) : |f x| ≤ |B| := by
    by_cases hx : x ∈ tsupport f
    · exact (by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hB x hx : |f x| ≤ B).trans (le_abs_self B)
    · simp [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hx]
  have hgb (x : E) : |g x| ≤ |B| + |c| := by
    calc
      |g x| ≤ |f x| + |c| := by
        simpa only [g, sub_eq_add_neg, abs_neg] using abs_add_le (f x) (-c)
      _ ≤ |B| + |c| := add_le_add (hfb x) le_rfl
  have hga : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ := hg.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable
  have hgsq : Integrable (fun x => (g x)^2) μ :=
    (MemLp.of_bound hga (|B| + |c|)
      (ae_of_all μ (fun x => by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hgb x)) :
      MemLp g 2 μ).integrable_sq
  have hgd : fderiv ℝ g = fderiv ℝ f := by
    funext x
    simp only [g, fderiv_sub_const]
  have hgc : HasCompactSupport (fderiv ℝ g) := hgd.symm ▸ hs.fderiv ℝ
  have hnorm (v : E → ℝ) (x : E) : ‖fderiv ℝ v x‖ = ‖gradient v x‖ := by
    rw [← toDual_gradient]
    exact (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).norm_map _
  obtain ⟨henergy, hdata⟩ := eventually_contDiff_and_integrable_sqrt_perturbation μ g hg hgb hgc
  have hentropyLimit := tendsto_integral_klFun_one_add_mul_div_sq μ g hga (ae_of_all μ hgb)
  have henergyLimit := (eventually_integrable_and_tendsto_sqrt_perturbation_energy μ g
    (hg.differentiable (by simp)) (ae_of_all μ hgb) henergy).2
  have hscaled : ∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ),
      (∫ x, _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (1 + e * g x) ∂μ) / e^2 ≤
        2 * C * ((∫ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y => Real.sqrt (1 + e * g y)) x‖^2 ∂μ) / e^2) := by
    filter_upwards [hdata.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds, self_mem_nhdsWithin] with e he he0
    have hne : e ≠ 0 := by simpa using he0
    obtain ⟨hpos, hu, hu2, hui, hud⟩ := he
    let p : E → ℝ := fun x => 1 + e * g x
    let u : E → ℝ := fun x => Real.sqrt (p x)
    have husq (x : E) : (u x)^2 = p x := Real.sq_sqrt (by
      have hx := hpos x
      dsimp [p]
      linarith)
    have hpi : Integrable p μ := (integrable_const 1).add (hgi.const_mul e)
    have hmass : (∫ x, p x ∂μ) = 1 := by
      rw [integral_add (integrable_const 1) (hgi.const_mul e), integral_const_mul, hmean]
      simp
    change Integrable (fun x => (u x)^2 * Real.log ((u x)^2)) μ at hui
    have hlog : Integrable (fun x => p x * Real.log (p x)) μ := by
      simpa only [husq] using hui
    have hkl : (∫ x, _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (p x) ∂μ) =
        ∫ x, p x * Real.log (p x) ∂μ := by
      simp only [_root_.InformationTheory.klFun_apply]
      have hplus : Integrable (fun x => p x * Real.log (p x) + 1) μ :=
        hlog.add (integrable_const 1)
      rw [integral_sub hplus hpi,
        integral_add hlog (integrable_const 1), hmass]
      simp
    change ContDiff ℝ ∞ u at hu
    change Integrable (fun x => ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖^2) μ at hud
    have hug : MemLp (gradient u) 2 μ :=
      (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm
        (continuous_gradient_of_contDiff_one (hu.of_le (by simp))).aestronglyMeasurable).mpr
        (by simpa only [hnorm u] using hud)
    have hle := logSobolev_of_compact_smooth_tests μ C hLSI u hu hu2 hug hui
    simp only [husq, hmass, Real.log_one, mul_zero, sub_zero] at hle
    change (∫ x, _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (p x) ∂μ) / e^2 ≤
      2 * C * ((∫ x, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖^2 ∂μ) / e^2)
    rw [hkl, ← mul_div_assoc]
    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by simpa only [hnorm u] using hle)
      (sq_pos_of_ne_zero hne).le
  have hlim := le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto hentropyLimit (henergyLimit.const_mul (2 * C)) hscaled
  have henergyf : Integrable (fun x => ‖gradient f x‖^2) μ := by
    simpa only [hgd, hnorm f] using henergy
  refine ⟨⟨hfi, hgsq, henergyf⟩, ?_⟩
  rw [Poincare.variance, Poincare.dirichletEnergy]
  change (∫ x, (g x)^2 ∂μ) ≤ C * ∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂μ
  simp only [hgd, hnorm f] at hlim
  linarith

mathematical_cores.question:
Let \(\mu\) be a Borel probability measure on a finite-dimensional real
Hilbert space. For every compactly supported smooth real \(v\), assume
\[
  \operatorname{Ent}_\mu(v^2)\le 2C\int\|\nabla v\|^2\,d\mu,
  \qquad
  \operatorname{Ent}_\mu(q)=\int q\log q\,d\mu
        -\Big(\int q\,d\mu\Big)\log\Big(\int q\,d\mu\Big),
\]
where \(0\log0=0\) and \(C\) is fixed. Prove by linearization that every
compactly supported smooth \(f\) satisfies
\[
  \operatorname{Var}_\mu(f)\le C\int\|\nabla f\|^2\,d\mu.
\]
Use the square root of a mass-one affine perturbation built from \(f\).
Justify its admissibility as an LSI test and justify the integrals and
limits. In particular, establish integrability of \(f\), its squared centered
value, and \(\|\nabla f\|^2\); do not assume that \(f\) already has mean zero.

rubric.criterion: Integrability and centering: Establishes integrability of the original \(f\), its centered square, and \(\|\nabla f\|^2\); centers \(f\) and proves mass one for a positive small affine perturbation. One argument may cover multiple integrability obligations. Derivative support is a valid route, not a mandatory phrase.

Legitimate LSI test domain: Justifies the use of the actual square-root test via cutoffs or another valid domain argument without assuming a stronger LSI. In a library-assisted run, an allowed domain extension plus checked hypotheses suffices.

Entropy limit: Justifies entropy normalization, cancellation of the linear term, and the \(1/2\) coefficient using domination or an equivalent integrated uniform remainder. Direct expansion of \(p\log p\) is as valid as compensation.

Energy limit and PI: Justifies the genuine square-root energy limit with coefficient \(1/4\), passes the inequality using only positive squared parameters, recovers the original variance/gradient, and obtains \(C\) with no stronger premise.

mathematical_cores.source_note: Exercise 1.7, printed p.43 / PDF p.55; compact Euclidean test classes and normalization in §2.1.1, printed pp.48–49 / PDF pp.60–61
steps: Center without preserving support: Compact support and continuity make f bounded and integrable. Probability normalization makes the centered function mean-zero. Subtracting a constant can destroy compact support of the function, but the derivative retains compact support. \[\begin{gathered}g=f-\int f\,d\mu,\\\int g\,d\mu=0,\qquad Dg=Df.\end{gathered}\]

Justify the noncompact square-root test: For sufficiently small absolute parameter, bounded g makes the affine density lie between one half and three halves. Its square root is smooth. Mass and entropy integrands are integrable by boundedness, and the genuine gradient energy is integrable by the derivative formula and the compact support of Df. The previously proved cutoff extension, rather than the compact premise alone, makes this test legitimate. \[\begin{gathered}p_\varepsilon=1+\varepsilon g,\quad u_\varepsilon=\sqrt{p_\varepsilon},\\\nabla u_\varepsilon=\frac{\varepsilon\,\nabla g}{2\sqrt{p_\varepsilon}}.\end{gathered}\]

Normalize and compensate: The affine density has mass one. The homogeneous entropy normalization vanishes, and the integrated linear compensation also cancels. This step compares real integrals, not Radon–Nikodym laws. \[\begin{gathered}\int p_\varepsilon\,d\mu=1,\quad k(t)=t\log t+1-t,\\\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(u_\varepsilon^2)=\int k(p_\varepsilon)\,d\mu\\\le2C\int\|\nabla u_\varepsilon\|^2\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

Divide by ε² and take the two limits: For nonzero ε divide by its positive square. Taylor's integral remainder for k at 1 bounds its quotient by g² and gives pointwise limit g²/2. The energy quotient is bounded by half the squared gradient of g and tends to a quarter of it. Dominated convergence applies to both. Closedness of real order keeps the same constant; no division by C is used. \[\begin{gathered}\frac{\int k(p_\varepsilon)\,d\mu}{\varepsilon^2}\to\frac12\int g^2\,d\mu,\\\frac{\int\|\nabla u_\varepsilon\|^2\,d\mu}{\varepsilon^2}\to\frac14\int\|\nabla f\|^2\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedDensityPerturbation
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedPerturbationLaw
import Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.Lemmas

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology Asymptotics
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedDensityPerturbation
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.BoundedPerturbationLaw
example
    {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (f : X → ℝ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {M : ℝ}
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |f x| ≤ M) (hcenter : (∫ x, f x ∂μ) = 0) :
    let ν := fun e : ℝ => μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))
    (∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ),
      IsProbabilityMeasure (ν e) ∧ _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ < ⊤) ∧
    (fun e : ℝ => (_root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ).toReal -
      e ^ 2 * ((∫ x, f x ^ 2 ∂μ) / 2)) =o[𝓝 (0 : ℝ)] (fun e : ℝ => e ^ 2) := by
  let ν := fun e : ℝ => μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))
  let K := fun e : ℝ => (_root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ).toReal
  let Q := (∫ x, f x ^ 2 ∂μ) / 2
  let R := fun e : ℝ => K e - e ^ 2 * Q
  change (∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ),
    IsProbabilityMeasure (ν e) ∧ _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ < ⊤) ∧
    R =o[𝓝 (0 : ℝ)] (fun e : ℝ => e ^ 2)
  have hlaw := eventually_isProbabilityMeasure_and_klDiv_eq_one_add_mul μ f hf hbound hcenter
  constructor
  · filter_upwards [hlaw] with e he
    refine ⟨he.2.1, ?_⟩
    dsimp only [ν]
    rw [he.2.2]
    exact ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top
  have hreal : ∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), K e =
      ∫ x, _root_.InformationTheory.klFun (1 + e * f x) ∂μ := by
    filter_upwards [hlaw] with e he
    dsimp only [K, ν]
    rw [he.2.2, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal]
    exact integral_nonneg_of_ae (he.1.mono fun x hx =>
      _root_.InformationTheory.klFun_nonneg (by linarith))
  have hnorm : Tendsto (fun e : ℝ => K e / e ^ 2) (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 Q) :=
    (tendsto_integral_klFun_one_add_mul_div_sq μ f hf hbound).congr'
      ((hreal.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds).mono fun e he =>
        congrArg (fun z : ℝ => z / e ^ 2) he.symm)
  have hRdiv : Tendsto (fun e : ℝ => R e / e ^ 2) (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 0) := by
    have hsub := hnorm.sub (tendsto_const_nhds (x := Q) (f := 𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ)))
    rw [sub_self] at hsub
    apply hsub.congr'
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with e he
    have hne : e ≠ 0 := by simpa using he
    change K e / e ^ 2 - Q = (K e - e ^ 2 * Q) / e ^ 2
    rw [sub_div, mul_comm (e ^ 2) Q, mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ (pow_ne_zero 2 hne)]
  have hν0 : ν 0 = μ := by
    have hd : (fun x : X => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + (0 : ℝ) * f x)) = (1 : X → ENNReal) := by
      ext x
      simp
    change μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + (0 : ℝ) * f x)) = μ
    rw [hd, withDensity_one]
  have hR0 : R 0 = 0 := by
    simp [R, K, hν0, _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv_self]
  apply Asymptotics.isLittleO_of_tendsto
  · intro e he
    have he0 : e = 0 := by
      by_contra hne
      exact (pow_ne_zero 2 hne) he

mathematical_cores.question:
Let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on a measurable space, and let \(f\) be
a real a.e. strongly measurable function such that \(|f|\le M\) almost
everywhere for some finite \(M\) and \(\int f\,d\mu=0\). For real
\(\varepsilon\), put \(d\nu_\varepsilon=(1+\varepsilon f)_+\,d\mu\).

For probability laws, use canonical extended-real KL: it is \(+\infty\)
without absolute continuity; otherwise it is the extended integral
\(\int r\log r\,d\mu\), where \(r=d\nu/d\mu\) and \(0\log0=0\).
Prove that for all sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\), including zero,
\(\nu_\varepsilon\) is a probability and its canonical KL relative to
\(\mu\) is finite. For its ordinary real value \(K_\varepsilon\) after
this finiteness is established, prove
\[
 K_\varepsilon=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\int f^2\,d\mu+o(\varepsilon^2)
 \qquad(\varepsilon\to0).
\]
Account for the actual probability law and justify passing the expansion
through the integral. The limit is two-sided.

rubric.criterion: Local law: Justifies a measurable density up to a null set, eventual a.e. positivity including degenerate bounds, exact mass one, absolute continuity and the actual density relative to \(\mu\). An argument uniform in the bound need not treat \(M=0\) separately.

Finite canonical KL: Establishes the genuine extended-real finiteness from the domain and integrability of the density entropy, or an equivalent valid formula, before interpreting the real value. An identity for a totalized real conversion alone is insufficient.

Quadratic coefficient: Cancels the integrated linear term (with or without a compensated function) and establishes the \(1/2\) coefficient with a legitimate integrable envelope or uniform remainder. Finiteness alone is not this limit.

Full remainder: Proves the two-sided little-o and the zero remainder at \(\nu_0=\mu\); a proof applying the positive-side estimate also to \(-f\) is valid. An all-small-parameters argument may include zero implicitly. A quotient value assigned at zero is not convergence evidence.

steps: Construct the probability law: Essential boundedness puts the affine density in [1/2,3/2] a.e. for small |ε|, including the degenerate bound M=0. Centering and reference probability give mass one. The density is positive a.e.; withDensity of its ENNReal image yields the actual probability measure and its a.e. Radon–Nikodym derivative. \[\begin{gathered}p_\varepsilon=1+\varepsilon f,\quad \tfrac12\le p_\varepsilon\le\tfrac32\ \text{a.e.},\\\int p_\varepsilon\,d\mu=1,\quad d\nu_\varepsilon=p_\varepsilon\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

Prove finite extended-real KL first: The canonical KL is the nonnegative-real image of the compensated integral, which is finite. That establishes KL < ∞ independently of toReal. Nonnegativity of k makes its integral nonnegative, so the real KL then equals the actual real integral. \[\begin{gathered}k(t)=t\log t+1-t,\\K_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ext}}=\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\int k(p_\varepsilon)\,d\mu\right)<\infty,\\K_\varepsilon=(K_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ext}})_{\mathbb R}=\int k(p_\varepsilon)\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

Use the compensated-integral limit: At 1, k and its first derivative vanish. Taylor's integral remainder divides by ε² only off zero; the positive segment gives the f² envelope, and the limit is f²/2. The analytic parent proves this scalar coefficient and domination, then passes the integral to the limit. \[\begin{gathered}\frac{k(1+\varepsilon f)}{\varepsilon^2}=f^2\int_0^1\frac{1-s}{1+s\varepsilon f}\,ds,\\0\le\frac{k(1+\varepsilon f)}{\varepsilon^2}\le f^2,\\\frac{K_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon^2}\to\frac12\int f^2\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

Include the exact zero endpoint: At ε=0 the density is one, so the tilted law equals μ and its KL is zero. The remainder vanishes there. Combine the punctured quotient limit with the exact endpoint to obtain little-o on the full neighborhood. \[\begin{gathered}R_\varepsilon=K_\varepsilon-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\int f^2\,d\mu,\\R_0=0,\qquad R_\varepsilon=o(\varepsilon^2).\end{gathered}\]

case-1.assumptions: The log-Sobolev hypothesis is ∫ v(x)^2 log(v(x)^2) dμ(x) − (∫ v(x)^2 dμ(x)) log(∫ v(x)^2 dμ(x)) ≤ 2 C ∫ ‖∇v(x)‖² dμ(x) for every C∞ compactly supported v. Independently, f is C∞ and has compact support. There is no separate admissibility assumption on f, no assumption of a density for μ, and no explicit sign assumption on C.
case-1.conclusion: Both Poincare.Admissible μ f and Poincare.variance μ f ≤ C · Poincare.dirichletEnergy μ f hold. Admissibility says that f, x ↦ (f(x) − ∫ f dμ)^2, and x ↦ ‖∇f(x)‖² are each μ-integrable. In particular the inequality is ∫ (f − ∫ f dμ)^2 dμ ≤ C ∫ ‖∇f‖² dμ with the stated integrability, not merely an inequality between totalized integral expressions.
case-1.constants: The real parameter C appears as 2 C in the entropy inequality and exactly C in the Poincaré inequality. No separate positivity, optimality, or sharpness of C is asserted.
case-1.domains: E is an implicitly quantified type carrying a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner product space structure, completeness, finite dimension over ℝ, a measurable space structure, and the BorelSpace compatibility instance. μ is a measure on this Borel space with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance. Both f and the tests v map E to ℝ. All displayed integrals are against μ over E.
case-1.objects: A probability measure μ on E, a real constant C, real-valued smooth compactly supported test functions v, and a real-valued smooth compactly supported function f. For a real-valued g let m_g = ∫ g dμ. The conclusion uses variance ∫ (f − m_f)^2 dμ and Dirichlet energy ∫ ‖∇f‖² dμ, with the genuine inner-product gradient ∇.
case-1.quantifiers: For every E with the listed typeclass instances, every μ with the probability instance, and every C : ℝ, if the displayed log-Sobolev bound holds for every v : E → ℝ that is C∞ and has compact support, then for every f : E → ℝ that is C∞ and has compact support the stated conjunction holds. The same C and μ are used throughout.
case-1.senses: C∞ means real Fréchet smoothness at every finite order, not analyticity. Compact support is compactness of the closure of the nonzero set. The log is the real natural logarithm, with the entropy terms using the zero convention (including the zero test). The centered variance is taken under μ, and the gradient is the genuine gradient defined by the inner product, not a weak or metric slope. The conclusion concerns smooth compactly supported f only; it does not extend the inequality to every admissible f or assert a converse.

case-2.assumptions: f is μ-almost-everywhere strongly measurable, |f(x)| ≤ M for μ-almost every x, and its integral ∫ f dμ equals zero. Neither everywhere measurability nor a pointwise bound is assumed. Boundedness together with the probability and measurability assumptions makes f and f² integrable; no separate integrability, positivity of M, or nonzero second moment is assumed.
case-2.conclusion: Both claims hold: (1) eventually for e in 𝓝 0, ν(e) is a probability measure and klDiv(ν(e), μ) < ⊤; (2) the real residual r(e) = klDiv(ν(e), μ).toReal − e²[(∫ f(x)² dμ(x))/2] satisfies r = o[𝓝 0](e ↦ e²). Equivalently in the eventual probability and finite-divergence regime, the ordinary KL divergence has the expansion e²(∫ f² dμ)/2 + o(e²).
case-2.constants: M is a real essential absolute bound, not the expansion coefficient. The quadratic coefficient is exactly (∫ f² dμ)/2, half the second moment and, by centering, half the variance. There is no constant or linear term in the expansion. No explicit neighborhood radius or remainder constant is claimed.
case-2.domains: X is an implicitly quantified type with a MeasurableSpace instance, with no required topology, vector space, or Borel structure. μ is a measure on X with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance. f : X → ℝ and M, e : ℝ. The density takes values in the extended nonnegative reals and the asymptotic uses the real neighborhood filter 𝓝 (0 : ℝ).
case-2.objects: A probability measure μ on X; a real-valued function f on X; a real bound M; a real perturbation parameter e; and ν(e) = μ.withDensity(x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal(1 + e f(x))). The divergence is InformationTheory.klDiv(ν(e), μ) in that order, with extended nonnegative real values; the expansion uses its toReal value.
case-2.quantifiers: For every X with the listed measurable structure, every probability μ on X, every f : X → ℝ satisfying the hypotheses, and every implicit M : ℝ witnessing the bound, define ν for all real e. There is a neighborhood of zero on which each e simultaneously gives a probability ν(e) and finite divergence. Separately, the little-o claim quantifies over every tolerance η > 0 with a possibly η-dependent neighborhood of zero.
case-2.senses: withDensity is relative to μ and ENNReal.ofReal clips negative real values to zero, so the definition does not assume an everywhere nonnegative untruncated affine density. Near zero, essential boundedness does make 1 + e f positive μ-almost everywhere, and centering yields unit mass. The neighborhood is two-sided and includes zero. The little-o statement means that for each η > 0, |r(e)| ≤ η |e|² eventually in that full neighborhood, hence r(e)/e² tends to zero on the punctured neighborhood as well. Only eventual finiteness makes toReal an ordinary finite KL value there; the proposition gives no all-e probability or finiteness claim, exact quadratic identity, uniform asymptotic over f, or higher-order bound.
